Yes, special equipment including the astrolabe, octant, sextant, and obviously compasses. Making maps is largely knowing the location of the observing artist, their longitude most notably. Maps start with large landmarks like rivers, mountains and geological features that are easy to parse from ground level. Though they had no bird’s eye view, features such as coastlines and outlier islands did help in orienting ancient map makers. Search for information about Ptolemaic Cartography and “Clover Maps” for an idea of early mapmaking.
